blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Compliance culture at executive level is less about rules and more about tone. Every organisation learns, very quickly, which kinds of questions its leaders are genuinely willing to answer and which they quietly prefer not to hear. A leadership team that asks 'is this definitely correct?' at every doubt creates a culture in which doubt is surfaced early. A leadership team that sighs when compliance raises a concern creates the opposite — one in which concerns are quietly buried, surfacing only when it is too late.

To the extent that tone is set by the senior team, it is the senior team's responsibility to set it deliberately. Provided that the CEO and CFO treat compliance questions with genuine patience, the rest of the organisation learns that the questions are welcome.

Although regulators rarely see this culture directly, they can feel it in the quality of interactions. A company whose compliance culture is strong does not need many conversations with its regulator. The conversations it does have, it handles calmly.

items.q: According to the text, compliance culture at executive level is mainly a matter of…
items.why: "Compliance culture at executive level is less about rules and more about tone."

items.q: What happens in a culture where leaders sigh when compliance raises a concern?
options: Concerns are quietly buried until it is too late
items.why: "concerns are quietly buried, surfacing only when it is too late."

items.q: According to the text, why can regulators still sense a company's compliance culture?
options: Because the culture is published openly
Because they feel it in the quality of interactions
Because whistleblowers report it to them
items.why: "Although regulators rarely see this culture directly, they can feel it in the quality of interactions."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A robust compliance manual matters more than how leaders respond to doubt.
The behaviour of senior leaders shapes what their teams choose to report.
A strong culture reduces the number of difficult regulator conversations.
Setting the right tone is a deliberate responsibility of the senior team.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que o tom, e não o manual de regras, é o fator decisivo.

items.q: That a strong-culture company 'handles calmly' the few conversations it has with its regulator suggests that…
options: calmness is unrelated to how issues are managed
regulators are lenient with well-known firms
issues are surfaced early enough to be dealt with without panic
items.why: Inferência: se as dúvidas afloram cedo, os problemas chegam ao regulador já tratáveis — daí a calma.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando o CFO. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I show you something you probably haven't noticed? Twice this morning, when compliance flagged a query, you sighed. Just a small sigh — but everyone in that room heard it, and they will remember it.

Here is what happens next. The analyst who raised the flag isn't going to bring you the next one. Not because she's careless, but because she read the room. She learned, in two seconds, which questions you actually want to hear. And the ones you don't want to hear are precisely the ones that end up costing us.

I'm not asking you to pretend. I'm asking you to be deliberate about it. When a concern surfaces, the most valuable thing you can do is treat it with genuine patience — ask 'is this definitely correct?' and mean it. That single habit changes what your team is willing to tell you.

Think about it this way. The tone you set is doing your quality control for you, every single day, whether you intend it or not. If you get this right, most of our regulator conversations simply won't need to happen. And the ones that do, we'll handle calmly, because nothing will have been buried.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What behaviour did Charlotte point out to the CFO?
options: He sighed when compliance flagged a query
items.why: "Twice this morning, when compliance flagged a query, you sighed."

items.q: According to Charlotte, why won't the analyst bring the next flag?
options: Because she read the room and learned which questions he wants to hear
Because she was moved to another team
items.why: "Not because she's careless, but because she read the room."

items.q: What single habit does Charlotte recommend?
options: Treating concerns with genuine patience and asking if they are definitely correct
items.why: "treat it with genuine patience — ask 'is this definitely correct?' and mean it."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by 'the tone you set is doing your quality control for you'?
options: The leader's everyday reactions shape what problems get surfaced
The CFO no longer needs any controls
items.why: Inferência: o comportamento diário do líder já filtra o que a equipe traz — funciona como controle de qualidade.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's approach in this conversation?
options: Purely theoretical, with no practical advice
Direct but constructive, offering a concrete change
items.why: Inferência: ela aponta o problema com franqueza, mas propõe um hábito prático e explica o ganho.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "When a concern surfaces, the leader's reaction decides whether it is dealt with or buried." To surface here means to…
options: come to light or become visible
items.why: Surface = aflorar, vir à tona — a preocupação torna-se visível.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A single ___ from the CFO taught the analyst that her question was unwelcome."
items.why: Sigh = suspiro; foi o gesto que sinalizou impaciência.

items.q: "It is the senior team's responsibility to set the tone deliberately." Deliberately means…
items.why: Deliberately = deliberadamente, de propósito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Regulators rarely see the culture ___, but they sense it in every exchange."
items.why: Directly = diretamente; eles não observam a cultura de forma direta.

items.q: Genuine patience in this context refers to…
options: a real, unfeigned willingness to hear the concern out
items.why: Genuine patience = paciência genuína — de verdade, não fingida.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre cultura de compliance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board must sign off on the compliance framework before it goes live." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new whistleblowing channel across all sites next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "When compliance flagged the deal, the CFO pushed back on the objection." He…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to strengthen the culture but never followed through." They…
options: failed to see it through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "A polite reply that no one believes won't move the needle on how safe people feel raising concerns." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
